elements.evidence: The clause expressly grants the licence to Customer and “its Affiliates.”

elements.element: Licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly includes “contractors acting on Customer's behalf.”
The clause contains no perpetual-duration language and does not address paid-up licences.
The clause does not make paid-up licences irrevocable; instead, it states that the licence is revocable as provided in Section 13.3.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for material breach.
elements.evidence: The clause refers to Section 13.3 but does not operatively state that termination is limited to material breach. The non-operative margin comment cannot establish Section 13.3's terms.

elements.element: A subscription licence may be terminated for material breach only if that breach remains uncured.
elements.evidence: No uncured-breach requirement appears in the rendered clause, and Section 13.3's operative text has not been supplied.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: The licence remains expressly “non-transferable,” with no exception for successors.

elements.element: Affiliates are covered on written notice from Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause grants Affiliates immediate, unconditional coverage without requiring written notice, which is broader than coverage available upon written notice.

elements.element: Licence is transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
elements.evidence: The clause remains expressly non-transferable and contains no M&A-successor exception.

result.reason: The redline successfully adds Affiliates and contractors and removes Vendor's express sole-discretion revocation right, but it does not establish the required paid-up licence duration or irrevocability, does not demonstrate the required material-breach and cure limits for subscriptions, and affirmatively retains non-transferability without any successor exception. It therefore reaches neither a complete preferred nor fallback position. The changes are otherwise concise and do not visibly disturb unrelated commercial terms, although reliance on an unavailable Section 13.3 prevents verification of the termination protection.
